gates.evidence: At full-frame thumbnail and native scale the separate assembly reads as a manufactured robot arm with upper segment, large elbow, open metal forearm, wrist and mechanical hand beside a distinct robot chassis. It is not merely scattered metal or a human arm covering.

The upper shell joins a large round elbow, its open forearm rail/cylinder assembly continues to a distinct wrist collar and articulated hand. The major mechanical structure is connected and coherent; surface wear and bolt differences are incidental.

The woman holds a driver whose visible tip meets the wrist-region fastener while the other hand stabilizes the exposed mid-forearm frame on bench supports. Both repair targets remain present and active in the same image; contact was not transferred to the robot palm or removed. This interaction match does not waive the separate full human-chain requirement.

The visible driver grip, seated tip and supporting fingers on the bare rail are coherent with distinct boundaries. The complete support-hand wrist/forearm connection is hidden behind the frame between the sleeve patch and the visible palm/fingers, so the testcase requirement for both principal human hand/arm chains is not fully observable. This is an observability failure, not a diagnosis of impossible unseen anatomy.
